subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: How long does the Earth take to complete one rotation on its axis?
questions.explain: The Earth rotates once on its axis every 24 hours, giving the cycle of day and night.

questions.q: How long does the Earth take to make one complete orbit of the Sun?
questions.explain: The Earth orbits the Sun once every 365.25 days, which is one year.

questions.q: What is the main cause of day and night on the Earth?
options: The rotation of the Earth on its axis
The orbit of the Earth around the Sun
The orbit of the Moon around the Earth
The changing distance between the Earth and the Sun
questions.explain: As the Earth spins on its axis, the side facing the Sun has day and the side facing away has night.

questions.q: Which shows the correct order of the planets outward from the Sun?
options: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
Venus, Mercury, Earth, Mars, Saturn, Jupiter, Neptune, Uranus
Mercury, Earth, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus
Mars, Venus, Earth, Mercury, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune
questions.explain: The eight planets in order from the Sun are Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune.

questions.q: The asteroid belt (minor planets) is mainly found between the orbits of which two planets?
questions.explain: Most asteroids orbit the Sun in a belt lying between Mars and Jupiter.

questions.q: What keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
options: The gravitational attraction of the Sun
The magnetic field of the Sun
The electrostatic force from the Sun
The nuclear force from the Sun
questions.explain: The Sun's gravitational field provides the force that holds the planets in their orbits.

questions.q: Which four bodies are the gas giant planets of the Solar System?
questions.explain: The four large outer planets, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus and Neptune, are the gas giants; the inner four are rocky.

questions.q: Why do planets closer to the Sun move at higher orbital speeds than planets further away?
options: The Sun's gravitational field is stronger nearer to the Sun
The Sun's gravitational field is weaker nearer to the Sun
questions.explain: A stronger gravitational field near the Sun requires a higher orbital speed, so inner planets travel faster.

questions.q: A planet orbits the Sun at a radius of 1.5 x 10^11 m with a period of 3.0 x 10^7 s. Using v = 2 pi r / T, what is its orbital speed?
The Moon orbits the Earth at a radius of 3.8 x 10^8 m with a period of 2.4 x 10^6 s. Using v = 2 pi r / T, what is its orbital speed?
The Sun is mainly composed of which two elements?
questions.explain: The Sun, like most stars, is made up mostly of hydrogen and helium.

questions.q: A light-year is approximately equal to which distance?
questions.explain: A light-year is the distance light travels in one year, about 9.5 x 10^15 m.

questions.q: How does a star begin to form?
options: A nebula (cloud of dust and gas) collapses under its own gravity
A gas giant heats up until it ignites
A supernova compresses interstellar dust into a solid
questions.explain: Gravitational attraction pulls together the dust and gas of a nebula, forming a protostar and then a stable star.

questions.q: Which process releases energy in a stable (main-sequence) star such as the Sun?
options: Nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium
questions.explain: A stable star releases energy by fusing hydrogen nuclei into helium in its core.

questions.q: Which sequence describes the life cycle of a star much more massive than the Sun?
options: Nebula, stable star, red supergiant, supernova, neutron star or black hole
Nebula, stable star, red giant, white dwarf, black dwarf
Nebula, red dwarf, white dwarf, supernova, black hole
Stable star, red giant, supernova, planet, nebula
questions.explain: A very massive star swells into a red supergiant, explodes as a supernova, and leaves a neutron star or black hole.

questions.q: Where are elements heavier than iron mainly formed?
options: During normal fusion in a stable star
In the cold gas of a nebula
In the core of a red giant
questions.explain: Fusion in stars forms elements up to iron; elements heavier than iron are created in supernova explosions.

questions.q: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our Sun?
questions.explain: The Sun is one of many billions of stars that make up the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.q: Light from distant galaxies is redshifted. What does this provide evidence for?
questions.explain: Redshift shows distant galaxies are moving away from us, which is evidence that the Universe is expanding.

questions.q: Using v = H0 d with a Hubble constant of 2.2 x 10^-18 per second, what is the speed of a galaxy at a distance of 4.0 x 10^24 m?
An estimate of the age of the Universe is 1/H0. Using H0 = 2.2 x 10^-18 per second, this age is approximately:
questions.explain: 1 / (2.2 x 10^-18) = 4.5 x 10^17 s, giving an approximate age of the Universe.
